#1806. Mauricio Pochettino's first words at Tottenham, PSG, Chelsea and USA reveal Man United approach

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40

Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.

The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, with Michael Carrick's dismissal leaving Pochettino responsible for restoring confidence to a squad struggling for results.

The 54-year-old has inherited troubled teams before, although few appointments have offered such little preparation time before a fixture of this magnitude.

Looking back at his opening statements in four previous jobs reveals a recurring approach: Pochettino tends to publicly back the players he inherits, avoid making immediate transfer demands and emphasise the importance of collective responsibility.

Those principles have helped him transform some teams, but his experiences at PSG and Chelsea also demonstrate that they do not guarantee success.

When Pochettino arrived at Tottenham in 2014, the club were searching for stability after a disappointing campaign under Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood.

The Argentine had built his reputation at Southampton, where his energetic pressing system and ability to develop young players attracted considerable attention.

At his first major press engagement with Spurs, he resisted suggestions that widespread recruitment was necessary.

"We have an unbelievable squad with unbelievable players," Pochettino insisted.

"The most important thing is to develop our players and to provide the best team to play on the pitch."

His message was clear: improving the existing squad would take priority over demanding new signings.

That approach eventually helped Tottenham establish themselves among the Premier League's leading clubs.

Pochettino guided Spurs to second place in 2016-17 and reached the Champions League final in 2019, although he departed later that year without winning a trophy.

His appointment at PSG in January 2021 presented a different challenge.

Rather than developing a relatively young Premier League squad, Pochettino inherited a team containing established superstars, including Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.

During his introductory press conference, the Argentine again rejected the idea of imposing a rigid tactical system regardless of the available personnel.

Discussing the roles of Neymar and Mbappe, he explained that his responsibility was to find positions in which they could express their abilities and become decisive.

He also emphasised that a team's behaviour with and without possession mattered more than the formation displayed on paper.

The flexibility he promised was tested by the demands of managing an exceptionally talented squad.

Although PSG won Ligue 1 in 2021-22, Pochettino failed to deliver the Champions League success the club wanted and departed that summer.

Chelsea offered another rebuilding assignment in 2023.

The Blues had finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent campaign, and Pochettino was tasked with restoring their competitiveness following extensive changes to the playing squad.

At his first press conference, he acknowledged that performances alone would not satisfy expectations at Stamford Bridge.

The Argentine also expressed confidence in the club's sporting structure, explaining that he had accepted the owners' strategic plan rather than seeking greater authority over recruitment.

His Chelsea side eventually recovered to finish sixth and reached the EFL Cup final, but an inconsistent campaign ended with his departure by mutual consent in May 2024.

The experience demonstrated the difficulty of introducing a long-term playing philosophy while facing pressure for immediate results.

Pochettino's introductory press conference with the United States in September 2024 provided perhaps the clearest indication of the demands United's players can expect.

The former Tottenham manager made collective effort central to his philosophy, insisting that individual talent would only be effective within a properly organised team.

"But when we don't have the ball, we need to run, we need to be aggressive, we need to be competitive," he explained.

He also stressed that his coaching staff needed to create an environment in which players understood their responsibilities and could express their abilities.

That message carries particular relevance at Old Trafford.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches and have struggled to produce the collective intensity required to compete consistently.

Pochettino's preference for coordinated pressing could offer one route towards improvement, although implementing those principles will require time and careful management of the squad's physical condition.

His previous appointments suggest that he is unlikely to begin by publicly criticising individual players or demanding a major January overhaul.

At Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, his introductory message focused on working with the players already available, with recruitment generally left to the club's decision-makers.

That approach may be particularly important at United, where the relationship between the head coach and the sporting department will come under scrutiny as the January transfer window approaches.

Pochettino also has a record of improving young players, an asset for a squad featuring talents such as Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the circumstances surrounding his arrival leave little opportunity for a gradual introduction.

Unlike at Chelsea, where he benefited from a full pre-season, the Argentine has only a handful of training sessions before facing Liverpool.

United's position in the relegation zone also creates a more urgent challenge than the long-term projects he initially discussed at Tottenham or with the United States.

His opening press conferences across those four jobs suggest he will seek to protect his players publicly while demanding greater effort and discipline behind the scenes.

Whether those familiar principles can produce an immediate response will become clearer at Anfield, where Pochettino faces one of the most difficult possible introductions to life as Manchester United manager.

Loftus-Cheek’s Milan career is a frustrating one. He started off with a fantastic season in Serie A, but the same injury issues that had haunted him in England were present. Unfortunately, that’s the tale of his career in Italy, too.

His talent is very clearly there, but we’ve never had too much of a chance to see it on a consistent basis. It’s an unfortunate reality and this is likely to be the final full year of it.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, as Francesco Nasato relays on X, the Rossoneri could part ways with Loftus-Cheek in the new year. There are currently no renewal talks happening, so he’ll be able to leave as a free agent in the summer.

He’s currently sidelined, as the report continues, and hopes to return in late November if not early December, so time is running out for him to earn a renewal with the club. At this stage, though, it’s probably too high a mountain to climb.

An unfortunate position for everyone to be in, considering how impressive his first season was.

#1804. Egypt sack their manager for 'negative impact on team image' after he fainted when fight broke out between his TWO wives with punches and hair-pulling in a bar

Published: 13:16 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 13 November 2026

Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a new manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages.

Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media.

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast.

El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air.

Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women.

Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital.

En Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD

Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives

Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort

The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women

Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed.

His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health.

But in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children.

The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media.

The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team.

'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read.

Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'.

'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.'

Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place.

The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living.

Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children

Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages.

As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking.

Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under new head coach Ali Maher.

The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes.

When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had said: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'

#1803. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

#1802. Nottingham Forest: 21-year-old transfer target could be "eaten up" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30

Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

The Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window. Bournemouth are also said to be interested.

Bontempo, who turns 22 in January, has enjoyed a breakthrough year, contributing six goals and five assists in 50 appearances, and he earned his first Brazil call-up in September.

The lynchpin's contract runs until 2030, though, and speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery expressed doubts over whether the youngster could handle the step up to English football.

"He's had to grow up very quickly as a central midfielder with Santos," Vickery said. "His first year was a prolonged battle against relegation, and it is a team full of veterans, which puts a lot of strain on a young midfielder.

"He really has to cover the ground and link the play. He's a good little give-and-go midfielder.

"Premier League, now I have my doubts. He's around the six-foot mark, so he's not small, but he is physically quite flimsy.

"Everyone who comes from South American football to the Premier League says the same thing: 'You've got to play quicker. You must know what you're going to do with the ball before it comes.'

"In a Premier League midfield, I think he could be eaten up. I wouldn't see him as a player who's Premier League ready at the moment."

Rather than Bontempo, Vickery believes Forest should consider a familiar face in Danilo.

The 25-year-old broke his ankle on the opening day of the 2024-25 season against Bournemouth, and he joined Botafogo the following summer in a club-record deal worth around €22m (£19.2m).

Danilo was in superb form during the first half of 2026 and earned a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, but his hopes of securing a move to a Premier League side playing in the Champions League have yet to materialise.

"Forest could do a lot worse than get the left-footed, strong, quick-thinking, versatile Danilo back," Vickery added.

"At the moment, he's a better bet than Gabriel Bontempo, who is certainly one for the long term rather than now."

Danilo scored six goals and set up four more in 10 appearances for Nottingham Forest and was also linked with Manchester United during the summer transfer window.

#1800. Bruno Fernandes snubs second new contract offer from Man United in early headache for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino - with star free to talk to foreign clubs as early as January

Published: 18:28 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 14:42 EST, 13 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has rejected a new contract at Manchester United against the turbulent backdrop of the departure of head coach Michael Carrick.

The Manchester United captain publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Discussions are believed to have started between Fernandes and Man United over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But after an initial proposal from the club is thought to have been rejected by the midfield talisman, Fernandes has now snubbed a second deal with improved terms, in what could be an early headache for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Portuguese international's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract, but will continue talks over aspects including his salary and the length of his new deal as they are keen for him to stay.

Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second set of terms from Manchester United as the club seeks to pin him down to a new deal

The club captain inked his latest terms in 2024 with his contract set to expire next June

Man United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season, and announcing a new deal for Fernandes might have given the club an important boost of morale during a difficult international break.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Fernandes was publicly critical of his former head coach Michael Carrick last month but was later adamant that he had not held clear-the-air talks with him

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'

Fernandes' sabre-rattling was ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on Thursday after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco earlier this week to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday evening that staff members inside the club have been upset with the protracted sacking, which has been deemed disrespectful of Carrick's status as a club legend.

The source above believes that Pochettino should receive substantial financial backing from the club hierarchy when the winter transfer window opens in January.

The need for defensive reinforcements has grown increasingly urgent amid reports that Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez wants out of Old Trafford despite earning plaudits for his recent international displays.

#1798. This is exciting: Jurgen Klopp drops massive hint for Liverpool

Jurgen Klopp has dropped a major hint for Liverpool. It's one they simply have to take advantage of.

Jurgen Klopp left an incredible legacy at Liverpool and it's one that few have ever matched. It makes the decision to essentially move on very quickly from his time at the club a strange one.

The reaction to his exit was an overhaul. While that could be seen as an acceptance that things must be done differently without Klopp, it felt drastic. Especially as the squad he ultimately built did go on to win the Premier League.

But Liverpool tore it up the following summer. A large portion of that squad built for the future has already left, scattered across the Premier League and beyond after transfers.

They also immediately moved away from his high-intensity style of play and shifted the formation. Everything has changed very quickly - and not necessarily for the better. In fact, few could say it was for the better.

Hopefully, then, Liverpool can listen to him a bit now.

Klopp is now in charge of Germany, of course, and that means he's working closely with Florian Wirtz. Wirtz is widely regarded as the best German talent - just one that hasn't found his feet at Liverpool in over a year.

Not that you'd know that by watching him under Klopp. Wirtz quite plainly does look like the top talent, and he showed that again in a destruction of the Netherlands on Monday evening.

The playmaker scored twice and earned all sorts of plaudits. Deservedly so, too, as his two goals were fantastic.

“I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time,” Klopp said after the match.

“An extraordinary footballer. We have also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he is so vocal. He is the first pressing player, can press two players without getting tired.”

And there's the hint for Liverpool - they've found the right position. This is something the Reds haven't really done, with Arne Slot asking Wirtz to play the same congested position for almost the entirety of last season.

Even when it was apparent that it wouldn't work, he persisted. The result was Wirtz just not looking like Wirtz. Barely involved and unable to influence things.

Andoni Iraola has tried to fix that. Wirtz is afforded more space and more of a license to roam around the pitch, particularly between the lines. That gives us a better player, certainly, but there's still room to grow here.

But Klopp's hint is the key. It's about finding the right position for him - not just a no.10 but specifically with the team's shape and the options around him. Do that and you get an elite player.

The one Liverpool paid all that money for.

#1796. Mauricio Pochettino's January plans at Man Utd face 'early test' as USMNT star speaks out on Old Trafford links

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 00:35

Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie is reportedly unlikely to seal a return to the Premier League during the upcoming January transfer window.

Speculation surrounding a potential mid-season switch to England intensified after the 28-year-old recently discussed the prospect of United States internationals reuniting with Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.

Pochettino formally took the reins at Old Trafford following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, sparking immediate rumours that he could raid his former national team pool for winter reinforcements.

However, the Bianconeri have no intention of parting ways with the versatile American midway through the 2026-27 campaign.

According to Sky Sports News, Juventus head coach Luciano Spalletti is expected to publicly reiterate the club's firm stance against selling McKennie when he addresses the media this week.

The former Schalke man has remained an important figure in Turin this season, starting eight Serie A matches and contributing a goal alongside an assist in three Europa League outings.

McKennie is also understood to be completely settled in Italy after putting pen to paper on a lucrative contract extension in March that ties him to the Allianz Stadium until June 2030.

The midfielder himself recently moved to quell the growing transfer chatter, as reported by Fabrizio Romano: "I want to clarify I am not planning to leave Juventus. I am happy where I am. That's why I signed a new deal at Juve and I can't wait to continue here."

?⚪️⚫️ Weston McKennie: “I want to clarify I am not planning to leave Juventus”. “I am happy where I am. That’s why I signed a new deal at Juve and I can’t wait to continue there”. https://t.co/rkKvn9C2P9

While McKennie acknowledged that links between USMNT players and Man United are somewhat inevitable given Pochettino's familiarity with the squad, a reunion appears off the table for now.

The 28-year-old previously endured a brief six-month loan stint in the English top flight with Leeds United during the second half of the 2022-23 season before re-establishing himself in Serie A.

With Juventus holding all the cards due to his long-term agreement, the Red Devils will likely need to look elsewhere as they plot a crucial winter rebuild.

Pochettino is expected to be heavily backed in the January market as he bids to haul United up the Premier League table, with a new striker and a defender also thought to be high on the club's shortlist.

#1795. Journalist confirms Euro giants stance on Liverpool star

Liverpool made a lot of changes to their team in the summer.

In fact, even last year a lot of money was spent on trying to improve Liverpool's ranks.

Most people thought that the Reds would be unstoppable last term after bringing Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak in.

But, that was far from the case with the club finishing fifth in the Premier League, just a season after winning the title.

This forced Fenway Sports Group to make a change to their club and appoint Andoni Iraola.

Since then, things have got better but, as has been the case for a few years now, more players need to be brought in to bolster the Reds' ranks.

But, for them to do this, some of their own players may need to be moved on with many decisions still needing to be made.

Barcelona are not going to recall Ronald Araujo from his loan early

Ronald Araujo has probably been one of Liverpool's best signings this season.

If the defender was a permanent purchase, fans would have been very thankful that their club splashed the cash on him.

But, for now, he's on loan until the end of the season with the Reds having a €55 million option to buy in their favour.

Talk of Liverpool already making his stay permanent has emerged with some links with a return to Barcelona even arising.

However, thanks to an update from Ekrem Konur, the future of the Uruguayan has now been made a little more clear.

"Barcelona are not considering recalling Ronald Araújo from his loan spell at Liverpool in January," he wrote.

"The Catalan club continue to monitor the Uruguayan defender's development and performances closely.

"Barcelona are understood to be satisfied with Araújo's progress and value the regular playing time he is receiving at Liverpool.

"As a result, the club currently have no plans to activate a recall option during the January transfer window."

Liverpool need to weigh up their options before committing to Ronald Araujo

Even though Araujo's addition to Liverpool's starting XI has helped them out massively, the Reds can't just focus on him as their only option.

They're one of the biggest teams in the world and, with the way that things are going at the moment, they're also going to qualify for the Champions League.

Several different players such as Murillo, Pierre Kalulu and Nico Schlotterbeck have all emerged as potential options for Liverpool.

So, with this amount of talent available to them, why would they stick with just one option?

Obviously, if he continues with this purple patch of form he finds himself in, it'll be a no-brainer but, as has been the case since the start of the season, the €55 million option to buy does feel quite steep.

Here's hoping that a decision is made soon so that fans can understand what Liverpool's squad will look like next term.

#1794. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1793. Jurgen Klopp reveals he confronted Germany star over controversial crown celebration with links to 'anti-LGBTQ+ group' - and promises he won't repeat it

Published: 12:42 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 15:09 EST, 13 November 2026

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp insists midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a controversial goal celebration after opposition from supporters.

Nmecha, a Christian player for Borussia Dortmund, was criticised last weekend for celebrating scoring by lowering an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch.

The celebration - called 'The King's Return' - was popularised by an evangelical network of footballers called Ballers in God, which counts prominent Premier League players among its members. It is supposed to represent the idea of submission to God.

But an investigation by German outlets found that the campaign website for 'The King's Return' linked to a chat service run by an organisation called Groundwire, where counsellors shared anti-homosexual views and described abortion as 'Satan's Plan'. Daily Mail Sport encountered similar views when consulting the service.

Nmecha has maintained that his message was one of love, but after a huge outcry in Germany - and talks with Klopp and national team sporting director Rudi Voller - he will not adopt the celebration again.

Klopp said: 'It was a big ⁠issue. I saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time. But then it all kicked off.

Felix Nmecha has vowed not to repeat his 'King's Return' celebration after a huge outcry

He was called into a meeting with Jurgen Klopp and Germany's sporting director Rudi Voller for the celebration which is connected with evangelical Christian group Ballers in God

'As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

'I have known Felix Nmecha for a few months, and I can say that he is a very friendly young man, who is warm and open, and always spreads positive energy when he is with us.

'I confronted him with all the things you might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.

'For me ⁠the most important issue was settled. Then I said "how do we do it with the goal ⁠celebration?" He will not be celebrating like that.'

A vocal section of Dortmund fans opposed the club signing Nmecha from Wolfsburg in 2023 after he had shared anti-homosexual and anti-transgender posts.

Ballers in God was founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock and brings together a wide range of Christian players from across the pyramid with weekly sessions.

While the organisation does not hold an explicit stance on LGBTQ+ issues, their Instagram account did celebrate the end of the Rainbow Laces campaign in the Premier League last year.

In response to the Nmecha story, they wrote: 'We are encouraged by player-led movements such as The King's Return, where footballers themselves take the initiative to express their faith in Jesus.

Klopp says Nmecha told him he 'loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone'

'Our desire is not only to share our hope, but to demonstrate love and respect towards everyone, including those who do not share our beliefs.

'Our focus has always been, and will always be, to point people to Jesus with grace and love.'

Nmecha said: 'My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.'

Back at Dortmund, Nmecha, 26, still faces scrutiny. A supporters' group claimed that his celebration clashed with club values and he has been reprimanded by senior figures.

The club's president, Hans-Joachim Watzke, said: 'The fan department has every right to start a discussion like this. I was at their annual general meeting on Monday. It was clear that those who were bothered by parts of his celebration were in a significant majority. So you have to take it seriously and discuss it.

'If he scores a goal and points his index fingers upwards, everyone knows he wants to thank God. He is also welcome to make the sign of the cross.

'But placing the crown on the grass - that is, of course, somewhat linked to Ballers in God. I don’t even want to judge it. When I look at what they stand for, Borussia Dortmund’s code of core values and Ballers in God’s fundamental outlook are not entirely compatible. We don’t want that in our living room.

'I told him: "Felix, if you sense that it is dividing the fans, perhaps you will also realise that you shouldn’t do it any more." He wants to think about it. We had a wonderful conversation with him. We had a one-hour video call. That is where we are now, and he will think about it. I hope we can find a sensible solution.

'I like Felix Nmecha very much. We have a very, very good relationship and speak frequently. As a practising Catholic, I am the last person who would want to forbid someone from praying. That is not what this is about at all. It is legitimate, too. The only question we are discussing with him is the second part of his celebration.'

#1790. Report: Manchester United lead Liverpool in transfer race for £15m forward

Liverpool and Manchester United have been linked with a lot of the same players over the last few months.

Thanks to this, no matter how they're performing or how they performed the season before, they can always attract some of the biggest stars.

However, with how insane the transfer market is at the moment, clubs are now trying to find talented young players before they reach their peak.

Not only does this allow them to develop young talent but, it also means that they don't have to spend an arm and a leg on new players.

Recently, this transfer regime has become standard across the board and now, the Reds are going to have to try their best to beat their arch-rivals to the transfer of this forward.

Liverpool are trailing behind Manchester United for the transfer of Gabriel Rajkovic

Liverpool's main focus over the last couple of transfer windows has been improving their attack.

Mohamed Salah exited Anfield this summer and, even though Bradley Barcola was brought in to replace him, it still doesn't feel like their attack is right just yet.

And, with questions still surrounding the future of Rio Nguomoha and Cody Gakpo, nothing is set in stone.

Gabriel Rajkovic would be an out of the box signing for Liverpool

Over the last few years, Liverpool have tried to get better at signing youngsters before they become too expensive.

Right now, the Reds don't know how their team is going to look by the end of the season.

Last term, he featured in 18 and scored three.

So, even though he's incredibly young, it's clear that he's very talented and, if someone such as Liverpool ends up getting a deal over the line for him, they'll have a young, versatile attacker to add into their mix.

#1788. Report: European heavyweights enter transfer race for €100m Liverpool target

Liverpool are one of the most well-known football teams in the world.

The Anfield outfit have always been challenging for titles and silverware with the expectations of their fans rather high.

That is, especially after what Jurgen Klopp did while in charge of the club.

Since his departure, the Reds have won a Premier League title and have spent well over £600 million on new players.

And, while this may seem like a lot of money, many more changes need to take place before the Reds are back to their best.

So, not only does this mean more money needs to be spent but, it also means that Liverpool will have to cast their net far and wide to sign all the players that they need to.

Bayern Munich and Barcelona have joined the race for Aleksey Batrakov

One of the main problems Liverpool have faced this season is a lack of creativity.

The Anfield outfit have tried to rely on Florian Wirtz to create their chances but, he's constantly failed to meet expectations.

This has forced other players among the Reds' ranks to try and step up but, with the club currently sitting fourth in the table, that clearly hasn't worked out.

So, that's why a lot of Liverpool's recent transfer links have been with playmakers such as Aleksey Batrakov.

The Russian has been in fine form for Galatasaray this term with four of his seven goals coming in the Champions League.

In fact, his form has been so good that, according to Turkish outlet Takvim, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also entered the race for the 21-year-old.

"Galatasaray's 21-year-old Russian star, Aleksey Batrakov, has attracted the attention of leading European clubs," they wrote.

"While Barcelona and Bayern Munich are reportedly watching the young footballer closely, Galatasaray's management has taken steps to increase his €55 million release clause to €100 million."

Liverpool can't spend €100m on Aleksey Batrakov

Right now, Batrakov has a release clause worth around €55 million.

In pounds, that equates to around £45 million.

Obviously, this is a lot of money for a 21-year-old but, considering Liverpool spent £40 million on Milos Kerkez, it doesn't seem all that bad.

Since joining Galatasaray in the summer, Batrakov has contributed to 10 goals in 13 games.

The Turkish Super Lig outfit have mostly played him as a number 10 but, there has been the odd occasion when he was used as a number 8.

Compared to someone such as Wirtz or Dominik Szoboszlai, he may not seem as good but, from the games he's featured in this season, you can tell that the youngster has a bright future ahead of him.

Right now, it's unclear what Liverpool are going to do but, if Galatasaray do manage to up his release clause to €100 million that would be far too much money to risk on a relatively unproven youngster.

#1785. Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in TEARS as he speaks out on 'most difficult decision' to leave US for Man United after agreeing to replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss, and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

United confirmed that Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half-year contract to replace Michael Carrick, and will start work on Wednesday after staying on for a double-header against Haiti.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss

Pochettino spoke at a USMNT press conference after his move to Man United was confirmed

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after a 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

United are paying US Soccer more than £10million in compensation to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, and have allowed him to stay in charge for two more matches.

‘I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’

Pochettino, who will oversee his side's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti over the next week, insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT

Meanwhile, Carrick issued a statement following his sacking on Thursday after 10 months in charge.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

#1784. Opinion: Liverpool forced into €80m action over Real Madrid's Endrick

Now's your chance, Liverpool. It's time to act on Real Madrid's Endrick and make another statement signing.

Liverpool tried to sign Endrick from Real Madrid in the summer but it's one that fell apart for various reasons. Eventually, Jose Mourinho decided he didn't want to lose the player, while Endrick himself was never too keen on ending his time with Los Blancos.

But things were relatively close. Liverpool were far from the only club to try and sign him, too, it's expected that Endrick will command a lot of attention when he does decide to leave Real Madrid.

We imagine that will be soon. The Brazilian hasn't been afforded many opportunities at all across the beginning of this season and it certainly appears in reports that Real Madrid are open to letting him leave.

Whether that's permanently or on loan depends entirely on the deal offered. Real Madrid will be reluctant to entirely lose control of Endrick's future but the right price almost certainly tempts them.

Battle for Endrick startsCorriere dello Sport claims that the bidding for Endrick has essentially started. AC Milan are leading it with a massive push to sign the player and they're putting up exactly the kind of deal that Real Madrid would want. €60m up front with a further €10m in add-ons is already good for a player who hasn't made an impact for Los Blancos. But with an €80m buy-back? It's essentially stupid for Real Madrid to reject that. If Endrick works out, they buy him back and paid €10m in development costs. And if he doesn't fulfil his potential? They get €60m for an average player.

Corriere dello Sport claims that the bidding for Endrick has essentially started. AC Milan are leading it with a massive push to sign the player and they're putting up exactly the kind of deal that Real Madrid would want.

€60m up front with a further €10m in add-ons is already good for a player who hasn't made an impact for Los Blancos. But with an €80m buy-back? It's essentially stupid for Real Madrid to reject that.

If Endrick works out, they buy him back and paid €10m in development costs. And if he doesn't fulfil his potential? They get €60m for an average player.

The problem for Liverpool is that they'd never strike a deal like that. They'd never allow another club to control a player's future like that - so Endrick would be signed outright or not at all.

We'll say at this stage that we're enormous fans of Endrick. Our Value Adder model scores him incredibly highly and he's exactly the kind of player Liverpool could use - a left-footed attacker who both scores and creates.

Signing him would mean going above that €60m figure and probably getting close to that €80m range. And is he actually worth that? Potentially, there's no question he is.

So the real question becomes 'can Liverpool guarantee his development at Anfield?'. Now, that we're not totally convinced of, given the number of forwards already at the club. But Milan's bid forces them into action over that exact question.

And if they can guarantee it, then a bid should really follow.

#1782. Inter Miami vs Columbus Crew - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:53

Inter Miami begin their MLS Cup title defence on Saturday when they host the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in game one of that best-of-three series.

The defending champions finished second in the Eastern Conference by two points, drawing their final regular-season outing at home to Charlotte FC, 3-3, while the Crew snuck in as the seventh seed with a thrilling 4-3 win over the Chicago Fire.

Miami will hope to take the first step toward more history on Saturday as they aim to become the first Eastern Conference club this century to capture consecutive MLS Cups.

If they can pull it off, they would be the first MLS side to do so since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011 and 2012 and the second ever to achieve that feat in the East, after DC United..

Kily Gonzalez has seen his team drop points in three of their last four league encounters, though they have only suffered one defeat since October.

Thanks in large part to captain Lionel Messi, Miami led the regular season in goals with 80, one fewer than they managed a year ago.

The Herons also led the league in goals per match (2.4) and have netted three or more times in four of their last five post-season outings.

Saturday will mark the first time they meet Columbus in the playoffs, and Inter Miami having never lost a home game against the Crew.

A team that could barely buy a win at the start of the regular season could seemingly do no wrong down the stretch of it.

The Crew began 2026 without a win in their first five league games but will enter the playoffs as one of the hottest teams remaining, riding a six-match winning streak.

Laurent Courtois has unlocked this team’s scoring potential, with Columbus netting multiple times in nine straight MLS affairs, with three or more goals in four of those instances.

This weekend they can end a three-match playoff losing run away from home, having won just one post-season affair since lifting the MLS Cup in 2023.

As potent as they have been in front of goal lately, this side have rarely shown much defensive poise away from home, conceding three or more goals in seven MLS games this year outside of ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Columbus won their only previous playoff game in the Sunshine State, defeating Orlando City 2-0 in 2023 en route to winning the MLS Cup later that year.

A shoulder issue will likely keep Mateo Silvetti on the Miami sidelines on Saturday, while Tadeo Allende is dealing with a knee problem, Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear and Cesar Abadia is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Messi finished the regular season as the top goalscorer for a second year running, though it was Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul who netted for them on Decision Day.

There is one injury concern on the Columbus side heading into this encounter as Wessam Abou Ali is doubtful because of a knee injury.

Gonzalo Tapia notched a brace for the Crew against the Fire, with Anass Zaroury and Brais Mendez also scoring, with the latter netting the winner in stoppage time.

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Reguilon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Bangoura, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia

We often see these teams throw caution to the wind and play in an all-out attack mode, and if that happens, as we anticipate in game one, the home team is more likely to come out on top given their firepower.
